original.target_description: Rothman (2011), study 1: full primary paper not obtained. Publisher supplies abstract/references only; publisher PDF returned 403; OpenAlex supplied no OA full text and Lancaster record states full text unavailable.

replication.target_description: Study 1, L3 Portuguese learners with L1 English/L2 Spanish or L1 Spanish/L2 English: main effect of adjective position (preposed vs. postposed) on correct responses in the semantic interpretation task; two-way ANOVA with participant random intercept.

n.location: pp. 1443–1444 (PDF pp. 5–6), Participants; p. 1448 (PDF p. 10), semantic interpretation ANOVA
n.quote:
A total of 211 participants took part in the experiments, consisting of two total
           groups.
n.sample_role: Participants across two mirror-image L3 Portuguese groups (96 L1 English/L2 Spanish; 115 L1 Spanish/L2 English), semantic interpretation ANOVA.
n.exclusions: No task-specific exclusions stated; reported participant total is consistent with semantic interpretation denominator df 209.

es.location: p. 1448 (PDF p. 10), Replication of the original analysis, semantic interpretation position main effect
es.quote:
Like the collocation task, there was a main effect for position (pre vs. post) (F[1, 209] =
              8.41, p < .05).

p.location: p. 1448 (PDF p. 10), Replication of the original analysis, semantic interpretation position main effect
p.quote:
Like the collocation task, there was a main effect for position (pre vs. post) (F[1, 209] =

reported_success.location: p. 1450 (PDF p. 12), Discussion and Conclusion, paragraph 1; Table 2
reported_success.quote: Overall, the results of the two ANOVAs point to a partial replication of the original analysis.

notes: Reported success is the authors’ overall partial-replication verdict, mapped to mixed; it is not an effect-specific significance inference. Original statistics quoted secondhand by the replication were not substituted for the unavailable original primary paper.
